blocks.text: 30. Live MIDI Effect Reference
blocks.raw_html: 30. Live MIDI Effect Reference

blocks.text: Live comes with a selection of custom-designed, built-in MIDI effects. These effects can modify incoming MIDI pitch, length, and velocity data in various ways. You can use a MIDI effect on its own to add variation to a pattern or combine multiple MIDI effects to create more complex note sequences.

You can use a MIDI effect on its own to add variation to a pattern or combine multiple MIDI effects to create more complex note sequences.

blocks.text: All MIDI effects with pitch controls support scale awareness. When the Use Current Scale toggle in the device title bar is enabled, any pitch-related controls can be adjusted in scale degrees instead of semitones. This ensures that all note transpositions stay within a specific harmonic range.

blocks.text: 30.1 Arpeggiator
blocks.raw_html: 30.1 Arpeggiator

blocks.text: Arpeggiator creates rhythmical patterns using the notes of a chord or a single note. It offers a complete set of both standard and unique arpeggiator features.
blocks.raw_html: Arpeggiator creates rhythmical patterns using the notes of a chord or a single note. It offers a complete set of both standard and unique arpeggiator features.

blocks.text: Arpeggiators are a classic element in 80s synth music. The name originates from the musical concept of the arpeggio, in which the notes comprising a chord are played as a series rather than in unison. “Arpeggio” is derived from the Italian word “arpeggiare,” which refers to playing notes on a harp.

blocks.text: The arpeggiated pattern plays at the speed set by the Rate control, which uses either milliseconds or tempo-synced beat divisions, depending on which Sync/Free Rate toggle is selected.

blocks.text: You can transpose the pattern using the Distance and Steps controls. The Distance control sets the transposition in semitones or scale degrees, while the Steps control determines how many times the pattern is transposed. The pattern initially plays at its original pitch and then repeats at progressively higher transpositions when using positive Distance values or lower transpositions when using negative values. For example, when Distance is set to +12 st and Steps is set to 2, a pattern starting with C3 will play first at C3, then C4, and finally at C5.

blocks.text: The Gate control determines the length of the notes in the pattern as a percentage of the Rate value. Gate values above 100% result in notes that overlap, creating a legato effect.

blocks.text: When playing notes using a MIDI controller, you can enable the Hold switch to keep the pattern playing even after releasing the keys. The pattern will continue to repeat until another key is pressed. You can hold an initial set of keys and then press additional keys to add notes to a currently held pattern. To remove notes, play them a second time. This allows you to create a gradual buildup and rearrangement of the pattern over time.

blocks.text: The Pattern Offset control shifts the sequence of notes in the pattern by a specified number of steps. Imagine the pattern as a circle of notes that is played in a clockwise direction from a set start point — Pattern Offset effectively rotates this circle counterclockwise one note at a time, shifting the starting note. For example, if the offset is set to 1, the second note in the pattern plays first and the original first note plays last.

Setting Repeats to 1 or 2 can emulate the strumming of a guitar, for example. You can also combine different Repeats values with various Retrigger settings to create rhythmically generated arpeggios with pauses in between.

blocks.text: 30.2 CC Control
blocks.raw_html: 30.2 CC Control

blocks.text: CC Control lets you send MIDI CC messages to hardware devices. It features three fixed control knobs (Mod Wheel, Pitch Bend, Pressure), one customizable button for sending on/off or minimum/maximum values (Custom A), and twelve customizable control dials (Custom B - M).
blocks.raw_html: CC Control lets you send MIDI CC messages to hardware devices. It features three fixed control knobs (Mod Wheel, Pitch Bend, Pressure), one customizable button for sending on/off or minimum/maximum values (Custom A), and twelve customizable control dials (Custom B - M).

blocks.text: The device’s fixed control knobs function as follows:
blocks.raw_html: The device’s fixed control knobs function as follows:

blocks.text: Mod Wheel – Sets the amount of modulation being applied by the receiving device.
blocks.raw_html: Mod Wheel – Sets the amount of modulation being applied by the receiving device.

blocks.text: Pitch Bend – Sends out pitch bend data to the receiving device. Negative values adjust the range downward and positive values adjust the range upward.

blocks.text: Pressure – Sets the amount of channel pressure/aftertouch being applied by the receiving device.
blocks.raw_html: Pressure – Sets the amount of channel pressure/aftertouch being applied by the receiving device.

blocks.text: The Custom A button sends out on/off or minimum/maximum values, which can be toggled between by turning the button on or off. While intended for sending sustain/hold pedal messages (CC 64), this button can be assigned to any other MIDI parameter via its CC Type Chooser drop-down menu.

blocks.text: The Custom B - M controls can be renamed and assigned to any MIDI parameter via each control’s CC Type Chooser drop-down menu. Custom names and assignments for these controls are shown on Push and are saveable as presets, allowing for easy navigation and reuse. Parameter values can be set using automation lanes or modulated in real time via the device’s control dials, which can be useful both for structuring and improvising with performances.

Using Learn also makes it easy to identify which CC message an external controller is sending.

blocks.text: 30.3 Chord
blocks.raw_html: 30.3 Chord

blocks.text: As the name suggests, this effect creates a chord using the pitch of each incoming note along with up to six additional pitches.
blocks.raw_html: As the name suggests, this effect creates a chord using the pitch of each incoming note along with up to six additional pitches.

blocks.text: You can use the Shift 1-6 controls to assign which pitches are used to contribute to a chord from a range of ±36 semitones relative to the original note. For example, setting Shift 1 to +4 semitones and Shift 2 to +7 semitones yields a major chord in which the incoming note is the root. Pitches can be set in any order — it makes no difference which Shift control is used for which pitch. The LED next to each Shift knob flashes to indicate when its corresponding note is being played.

blocks.text: Note that the same pitch cannot be assigned to multiple Shift controls. For example, you cannot set both Shift 2 and Shift 3 to +8 st. If a pitch is already assigned to a Shift control, any additional assignments of the same pitch will be deactivated.

blocks.text: In addition to setting pitches manually, you can enable the Learn toggle in the device title bar to assign pitches by playing a chord on an external MIDI controller. To do so, hold the keys you want to include in the chord. The pitch of the first held key determines the root and is not assigned to a Shift control; any subsequent pitches are assigned to the Shift controls in order. You can add more pitches by holding new keys while keeping the original keys held. Once the desired pitches are assigned, deactivate the Learn toggle.

blocks.text: Velocity sets the velocity for a generated note. This is a relative control, with a range of 1% to 200%. At 100%, the velocity of the generated note matches the velocity of the incoming note. Varying the velocities between notes can introduce subtle overtones or dramatically alter a chord’s balance.

blocks.text: Chance sets the probability that a generated note will play when an incoming note is triggered. You can set the probability anywhere from 0% to 100%. At 100%, a note is generated for every incoming note.

You can add duplicate notes by enabling the Play Duplicate Notes When Strumming option in the device title bar’s context menu.

blocks.text: 30.4 Note Length
blocks.raw_html: 30.4 Note Length

blocks.text: Note Length alters the length of incoming MIDI notes. It can also be used to trigger notes from MIDI Note Off messages, instead of the usual Note On messages.
blocks.raw_html: Note Length alters the length of incoming MIDI notes. It can also be used to trigger notes from MIDI Note Off messages, instead of the usual Note On messages.

blocks.text: The Trigger Source toggle determines whether the device is triggered by Note On or Note Off messages. When set to Note On, the length of incoming notes is determined by the Gate and Length controls. The Gate control defines how the value set by the Length control is applied. At 100%, notes play for the total duration specified by the Length control. Setting Gate to 200% doubles the length, while setting it to 50% halves the length. You can use the Time Mode toggles to adjust the length in milliseconds or tempo-synced beat divisions.

At 100%, notes play for the total duration specified by the Length control. Setting Gate to 200% doubles the length, while setting it to 50% halves the length. You can use the Time Mode toggles to adjust the length in milliseconds or tempo-synced beat divisions.

blocks.text: When the device is set to trigger from a Note Off event (the moment a note is released), the timing of an incoming note is delayed by its length — meaning the note starts at the moment it would have stopped if triggered by a Note On message. Once the initial delay is reached, the timing specified by the Gate and Length controls is applied.

blocks.text: Release Velocity — Determines the velocity of the output note. The percentage sets the balance between the incoming note’s Note On and Note Off velocities. If your keyboard does not support MIDI Note Off velocity, you can leave this set to 0%.

blocks.text: Decay Time — Sets the time needed for an incoming note’s velocity to decay to zero. The decay begins immediately from the moment the device receives a Note On message. The value at the time of Note Off becomes the velocity of the output note.

blocks.text: Key Scale — Alters the length of output notes based on the pitch of incoming notes. At positive values, notes below C3 are made progressively longer, while notes above C3 are made shorter. Negative values invert this behavior.

blocks.text: You can enable the Latch toggle to activate note latching. When using Note On messages, triggered notes continue playing until the next Note On message is received. When using Note Off messages, notes are triggered once all keys (or a sustain pedal, if connected) are released and a new Note Off message is received. In both cases, the Gate and Length controls are deactivated, as the length of triggered notes depends on the Note On/Off messages. Additionally, the Release Velocity, Decay Time, and Key Scale controls are deactivated for Note Off messages.

blocks.text: 30.6 Random
blocks.raw_html: 30.6 Random

blocks.text: Random adds an element of unpredictability to note sequences by randomizing the pitch of incoming notes.
blocks.raw_html: Random adds an element of unpredictability to note sequences by randomizing the pitch of incoming notes.

blocks.text: The Chance control determines how likely it is that an incoming note’s pitch will be randomly altered. You can think of it as a dry/wet control for randomness.
blocks.raw_html: The Chance control determines how likely it is that an incoming note’s pitch will be randomly altered. You can think of it as a dry/wet control for randomness.

blocks.text: The random value that determines the pitch change is created by two variables: the Choices and Interval controls. The Choices control defines the number of possible pitches, ranging from 1 to 24. The Interval control defines the number of possible intervals between the pitches. The values of these two controls are multiplied to determine the total range of possible pitches relative to the incoming note.

The Choices control defines the number of possible pitches, ranging from 1 to 24. The Interval control defines the number of possible intervals between the pitches. The values of these two controls are multiplied to determine the total range of possible pitches relative to the incoming note.

blocks.text: For example, when Chance is set to 50%, Choices is set to 1, and Interval is set to 12, repeatedly playing C3 results in half of the notes playing at C3 and half at C4, in no particular order. If you swap the Choices and Interval values by setting Choices to 12 and Interval to 1, half of the notes will play at C3, while the other half will play at any note between C#3 and C4. owner_requirements.title: scale-aware pitch controls
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0003–0004).** Enabling Use Current Scale changes pitch controls from
semitones to scale degrees. Device-specific ownership of root/scale appears
below. **U:** absent clip/scale, out-of-scale input selection, tuning systems,
scale changes while notes sound, and rounding of nonintegral transpositions.

owner_requirements.title: Arpeggiator sequence styles
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0011–0020, 0026).** Style selects and displays a note pattern; previous
and next buttons cycle styles. Play Order follows input play order; Chord Trigger
repeats the held pitches together. Random continuously randomizes; Random Other
avoids reusing a note until the others have been used; Random Once repeats one
random ordering until incoming MIDI changes. Pattern Offset 1 starts at the
second pattern position and moves the former first to last. **U:** exact orders
for Up/Down/Converge/Diverge and all other styles, duplicate-pitch identity,
random seed/distribution, what changes invalidate Random Once, and offsets beyond
one cycle. A finite random test does not prove distribution or fairness.

owner_requirements.title: Arpeggiator rate, gate and transposition
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0021–0024).** Rate is milliseconds in Free or a tempo-synced division.
Gate expresses duration as a percentage of Rate; values over 100% overlap.
Distance is semitones or scale degrees; Steps counts successive transpositions
following the original pattern. Distance +12 st, Steps 2 gives original, +12,
+24. Negative Distance lowers successive repetitions. Root/Scale choosers set
local scale; Use Current Scale takes the clip scale and disables these choosers.
**U:** first event phase, exact division catalog, timing grid, gate rounding,
end-of-pattern overlaps, groove interaction and pitches beyond the MIDI range.

owner_requirements.title: Arpeggiator held set, retrigger and repetition
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0025, 0030–0035).** Hold keeps a pattern after physical release; adding
held keys adds pitches and playing a pitch a second time removes it as described
by the manual. Retrigger Off does not restart the pattern, Note restarts on a
new note, Beat restarts at Interval; the retrigger LED flashes. Repeats controls
pattern repetition; its documented default is infinite. **U:** replacement versus
addition when all physical keys are up (the manual also says repetition continues
until another key), pedal interaction, last-note removal, finite-repeat restart,
transport stop/jump and held-note retirement. The held-set ambiguity is retained,
not resolved by choosing an interpretation.

owner_requirements.title: Arpeggiator velocity and groove
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0027–0029, 0036–0037).** Groove selects swing influenced by Global
Groove Amount. Velocity enables Target/Decay; Decay is the time to Target.
Velocity Retrigger restarts the velocity slope when the pattern retriggers.
**U:** decay curve, event velocities, target-zero note suppression, groove
quantities, retrigger phase and behavior when toggled during a held pattern.

owner_requirements.title: CC Control event families
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0041–0049).** The three fixed controls produce modulation, pitch bend
and channel pressure; Pitch Bend has downward negative and upward positive
values. Custom A switches between on/off or minimum/maximum and can be assigned
through CC Type Chooser; CC64 sustain is its documented intended use. There are
12 customizable dials B–M. Pitch bend and pressure must be observed as their own
MIDI event families, not assumed to be 7-bit CC messages. **U:** numeric ranges,
wire encoding, channel choice, quantization, reset-to-center and repeated-value
suppression; this source does not supply their byte-level laws.

owner_requirements.title: CC Control assignment, Send and automation
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0050–0052).** B–M have custom names and assignments, shown on Push and
saveable as presets. Values can be automated or moved in real time. Bank toggles
show controls 1–8 or 9–16. Send outputs current MIDI CC values. Learn assigns
incoming CC data to a customizable control. Existing CC automation and outgoing
CC Control data merge. **U:** learning target selection, multi-message learning,
consumption versus forwarding, Send order/count and treatment of non-CC fixed
controls, duplicate assignments, same-time merge order, smoothing, preset-load
emission and hardware receipt. Preset storage is a documentary promise, not an
observed successful round trip.

owner_requirements.title: Chord pitches and duplicate shifts
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0056–0058).** An input note supplies the root and up to six additional
pitches with Shift 1–6 in −36..+36 st. +4 and +7 form the root major triad,
independent of which slots hold those values. Reassigning the same pitch to
another Shift deactivates that additional assignment. **U:** zero-shift slot
activation, collision with another input note, pitch overflow, note-off ownership
and simultaneous ordering.

owner_requirements.title: Chord learning
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0059).** With Learn enabled, the first held key is the root and consumes
no Shift; subsequent held pitches fill Shift slots in play order. Additional
held keys extend the learned chord; disabling Learn ends assignment.
**U:** more than six additions, release/repress, sustain, removal, monitoring
while learning, cancelling a partially learned chord and undo grouping.

owner_requirements.title: Chord dynamics and chance
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0060–0063).** Each generated note has relative Velocity 1%..200%; 100%
matches input velocity. Chance is 0%..100%, with 100% generating that note for
every input. **U:** velocity multiply rounding/clipping, chance seed/distribution
or correlation, and note-off behavior after a suppressed note. No finite trial
count is required to reproduce a probability proportion.

owner_requirements.title: Chord strum, scale and per-note events
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0064–0073).** Strum offers delays up to 400 ms between notes; positive
order is original then Shift1..Shift6, negative reverses it. The context option
allows duplicate notes when strumming. Positive Tension accelerates successive
strums; negative slows them. Crescendo raises or lowers successive velocities.
Use Current Scale selects degree shifts. Send Per Note Events to Generated Notes
extends MPE data to generated notes; with scale awareness, per-note bend follows
the clip scale. **U:** delay curve/exact timestamps, tension/crescendo arithmetic,
late note-offs during a pending strum, duplicate policy with Strum zero, expression
channel allocation and bend values.

owner_requirements.title: Note Length triggered on note-on
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0077–0078).** With Trigger Source Note On and Latch off, output duration
is Length multiplied by Gate/100; Gate 50%, 100%, 200% yields half, full, double
Length. Time Mode selects milliseconds or tempo divisions. **U:** exact start
latency, source note-off suppression, same-key retrigger, gate/length control
bounds and updating Length or tempo while an output note sounds.

owner_requirements.title: Note Length triggered on note-off
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0079).** With Note Off selected, the output note starts when its input
note is released, rather than at input note-on, and then uses Gate and Length.
**U:** unpaired release, simultaneous releases, sustain's effect with Latch off,
output note-off velocity and event-grid placement.

owner_requirements.title: Note Length release dynamics
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0080–0083).** In Note Off mode, Release Velocity blends input on/off
velocities. Decay begins at incoming note-on; its value at note-off sets output
velocity, reaching zero after Decay Time. Positive Key Scale lengthens notes
below C3 and shortens those above; negative reverses that relationship.
**U:** blend equation, decay shape, order of operations, pitch scaling law and
zero-velocity result. No numeric output oracle follows from the qualitative law.

owner_requirements.title: Note Length latch
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0084).** Note On latch sustains triggered notes until the next note-on.
Note Off latch depends on all keys/pedal being released and a new note-off.
Latch disables Gate and Length; in Note Off latch, Release Velocity, Decay Time
and Key Scale are also disabled. **U:** exact Note Off latch transition (especially
which release qualifies), chord release ordering, pedal and repeated-note cases.
The documented UI disablement is gradable; the ambiguous Note Off event sequence
is not assigned a fabricated oracle.

owner_requirements.title: Pitch transposition and step controls
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0088–0092).** Pitch offers ±128 st or ±30 scale degrees. Step Up/Down
changes Pitch by Step Width, 1..48 st or 1..30 degrees. Controls accept key/MIDI
mapping (mapping math belongs to the mapping spec). **U:** clipping/wrapping at
control bounds, overflowed outgoing keys, off-scale degree selection and effects
of an automated pitch change on already sounding notes.

owner_requirements.title: Pitch range modes
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0093–0097).** Lowest and Range define permitted pitches. Block drops
out-of-range notes and flashes its LED; Fold transposes them into range; Limit
moves below-range notes to the lower bound and above-range notes to the upper
bound. **U:** range width/end inclusion, filtering before versus after Pitch,
Fold interval and empty/one-note range. Cases use Pitch zero to avoid inventing
the processing order and avoid unproven exact upper endpoints.

owner_requirements.title: Random pitch selection and signs
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0101–0104, 0107–0114).** Chance controls probability of pitch alteration;
Choices has 1..24 possibilities and Interval controls their spacing. Add raises,
Sub lowers, Bi permits both; the +/0/− LEDs identify the direction. The documented
Random/Add example Choices 1, Interval 12, Chance 50% restricts outputs to C3 or
C4 for input C3. Choices12/Interval1 permits unaltered C3 or C#3..C4.
**U:** seed/distribution, finite proportions, exact Chance thresholds, Bi zero
handling and overflow. The examples authorize pitch-membership predicates only,
not a fixed random sequence or a 50/50 finite-sample test.

owner_requirements.title: Random Alt mode and contradictory examples
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0105).** Alt uses a cyclic order. Chance100% advances to the next step;
Chance0% outputs the incoming pitch. **U (M 0106):** a 12-choice example describes
C3 through C4 before reset (13 notes), while Choices2/Interval2 describes only
C3,D3 (2 notes). These cannot support a single generalized cycle-length formula.
Both setups are retained as ungraded cases; phase/reset and intermediate Chance
are unknown. No algorithm is inferred from the parameter names.

owner_requirements.title: Random with a scale
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0115).** Use Current Scale constrains generated pitches to the clip
scale. **U:** degree spacing with Interval, inclusion of off-scale dry notes,
scale changes during Alt and cross-note versus per-pitch cycle state.

owner_requirements.title: Scale matrix and root
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0119–0122).** Matrix columns select incoming notes and rows outgoing
notes; mapping C to D converts incoming Cs to Ds. Base/Scale Name choose the
mapping; Use Current Scale uses the clip root/scale and disables those choosers.
User mode permits moving or deleting highlighted assignments; deletion prevents
that input note from producing output. **U:** top/right 13th grid cell semantics,
selection gestures and mapping ordinal encodings. The manual calls it a 13×13
grid representing 12 notes; no extra note class is inferred.

owner_requirements.title: Scale User fold
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0124).** In User mode, Fold changes a mapped pitch when its distance
from input exceeds six semitones. The documented C3→A3 mapping becomes C3→A2.
**U:** exactly ±6, downward counterpart, transpose ordering and range edges.

owner_requirements.title: Scale transposition and selected range
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0123, 0125).** Transpose is ±36 st. Lowest C2, Range+36 applies mapping
to C2..B4 and leaves other notes alone; Transpose+7 applies within that same
range. **U:** arbitrary range interpretation, one-note/zero ranges, overflow,
range versus fold/transpose order outside this documented example.

owner_requirements.title: Velocity transfer and operation
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0129–0132).** Lowest/Range select the input velocity interval; Out Low/Hi
select the output interval. The displayed curve shows the transfer. Operation
chooses Note On, Note Off (Rel. Vel.) or both. Out Low80/Hi127 constrains outputs
to the higher range. **U:** exact transfer formula and rounding, velocity zero,
fractional upstream velocities, swapped ranges and off-event ownership.
The manual's “essentially bypassed” example authorizes no bit-identity claim.

owner_requirements.title: Velocity outside-range modes
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0133–0136).** Clip constrains incoming out-of-range velocities; Gate
removes out-of-range events and flashes its LED when blocking a note; Fixed sets
outgoing velocity to Out Hi regardless of incoming velocity. **U:** exact range
endpoint inclusion, whether a gated note-on suppresses its later note-off,
release-only Gate lifecycle and precedence of Fixed versus Random/curve controls.

owner_requirements.title: Velocity randomness and curve shaping
owner_requirements.contract:
**D12 (M 0137–0142).** Random modulates velocity within the output range; the
OutLow60/Hi127, Random50 example permits up/down changes of at most50 while
remaining in60..127. Positive Drive favors higher velocities; negative favors
lower. Positive Compand expands toward extremes; negative compresses toward the
middle. **U:** formulas, distribution, seed, correlation, curve sampling and
processing order. Shading represents the random range; it is not a distribution
measurement.

owner_requirements.title: device lifecycle and failures
owner_requirements.contract:

row.source_claim: LFO is an MPE Transformation that uses a low-frequency oscillator to set the value of one of three MPE parameters: pitch bend, slide, or pressure. The oscillator’s shape, rate, and global amplitude can all be customized using the Transformation’s parameters. The Target chooser lets you set Pitch Bend, Slide, or Pressure as a modulation target for the LFO. The LFO curve display shows the shape of the LFO used as a modulation source. The Envelope Attack and Decay sliders set the attack and decay of the oscillator’s amplitude envelope, relative to the total length of the oscillation. Note that the envelope’s attack and decay values influence each other. This means that if, for example, Attack is set to 100%, Decay is automatically reset to 0%. The Shape control adjusts the shape of the oscillator based on the shape selected in the Shape Type chooser. You can choose from the following four types: Sine, Square, Triangle, or Random. When Random is selected, the Reseed button can be used to generate new random shapes for the LFO. The Rate control sets the period of the oscillator in musical time, from 1 to 1/128. For example, setting the rate to 1 equates to 4 beats. The Time Shift slider below Rate shifts the LFO in time. Positive values delay the start of the oscillation and negative values adjust its phase. The Amount control sets the oscillator’s amplitude. When Pitch Bend is selected as the modulation target, Amount can be set to any value within double the clip’s current pitch bend range. For example, if the range is set to ±60 st, Amount can be set from -120 st to 120 st. When Slide or Pressure are selected, Amount can be set from -127 to 127. You can set the base value for the amplitude using the Amplitude Base slider below the Amount control. When Pitch Bend is selected as a modulation target, Amplitude Base can be set to any value within the clip’s current pitch bend range. For example, if the range is set to ±60 st, Amplitude Base can be set from -60 st to 60 st. When Slide or Pressure are selected, Amplitude Base can be set from -127 to 127. The MPE curve for the Pitch Bend modulation target is displayed in the MIDI Note Editor. You can also choose to display it below the MIDI Note Editor by activating the Pitch Bend expression lane, which can be helpful when working with folded notes. Modulation curves for Slide and Pressure are displayed in their respective expression lanes. Note that the modulation applied by the LFO Transformation is only displayed in the MPE Editor. When the MIDI Note Editor is open, the Transformation is applied, but the expression curves are not visible.

quotes.quote: Mode determines how the randomization occurs: Random assigns pitches in no particular order, while Alt cycles through pitches in a fixed round-robin order. The Chance control behaves differently in this mode: at 100%, the next output note will always be the next note in the sequence, while at 0%, the next output note will always be the incoming note.

For example, when Chance is set to 100%, Choices is set to 12, and Interval is set to 1, playing C3 once plays C3, and each successive C3 plays the next semitone higher until C4, at which point the cycle starts over from C3. When Chance is set to 100% and Choices and Interval are set to 2, incoming C3s alternate between C3 and D3. This behavior is ideal for simulating upbow and downbow alternation with stringed instruments, or alternating right- and left-hand drum samples.
